## Purpose
Combine the Zumper, Rentler and ApartmentList listings into one table with the same columns, then flag buildings that appear on more than one site.

## Read the saved data
```{r read}
zumper  = readr::read_csv("data/zumper_oxford_clean.csv")
rentler = readr::read_csv("data/rentler_oxford_clean.csv")
alist   = readr::read_csv("data/apartmentlist_oxford_raw.csv")
```

## Give every source the same columns
```{r standardize}
zumper |>
  dplyr::mutate(address = dplyr::if_else(stringr::str_detect(address, "^[0-9]+$"), building_name, address)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    source = "Zumper", name = dplyr::coalesce(building_name, address), address, company,
    property_type = dplyr::case_when(property_type_code == 13 ~ "House",
                                     property_type_code %in% c(4, 9) ~ "Apartment",
                                     TRUE ~ "Other"),
    price = min_price, price_max = max_price,
    bedrooms = min_bedrooms, bedrooms_max = max_bedrooms,
    bathrooms = min_bathrooms, sqft = min_sqft,
    lat, lng, description, link, scrape_date
  ) -> zumper_std

rentler |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    source = "Rentler", name = address, address, company = NA_character_,
    property_type = NA_character_,  # Rentler labels everything "Apartment", so we take type from Zumper
    price, price_max = price, bedrooms, bedrooms_max = bedrooms,
    bathrooms, sqft, lat, lng, description, link, scrape_date
  ) -> rentler_std

alist |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(url, "/oh/oxford/")) |>
  dplyr::distinct(url, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    source = "ApartmentList", name, address = name, company = NA_character_,
    property_type = NA_character_,
    price = offers.lowPrice, price_max = offers.highPrice,
    bedrooms = NA_real_, bedrooms_max = NA_real_, bathrooms = NA_real_, sqft = NA_real_,
    lat = NA_real_, lng = NA_real_, description = NA_character_,
    link = url, scrape_date
  ) -> alist_std
```

## Combine and flag buildings listed on more than one site
```{r combine}
make_key = function(x) {
  x |>
    stringr::str_to_lower() |>
    stringr::str_remove_all("\\.") |>
    stringr::str_squish() |>
    stringr::str_extract("^[0-9]+ ([nsew] )?[a-z]+")  # e.g. "321 s main"
}

building_info = zumper_std |>
  dplyr::mutate(addr_key = make_key(address)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(addr_key)) |>
  dplyr::distinct(addr_key, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(addr_key, company_z = company, type_z = property_type)

dplyr::bind_rows(zumper_std, rentler_std, alist_std) |>
  dplyr::mutate(addr_key = make_key(address)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(building_info, by = "addr_key") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    company       = dplyr::coalesce(company, company_z),
    property_type = dplyr::coalesce(property_type, type_z),
    priority      = dplyr::case_when(source == "Rentler" ~ 1, source == "Zumper" ~ 2, TRUE ~ 3)
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(addr_key) |>
  dplyr::mutate(n_sites = dplyr::n_distinct(source), best = min(priority)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_sites = dplyr::if_else(is.na(addr_key), 1L, n_sites),
    keep    = is.na(addr_key) | priority == best
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-company_z, -type_z, -priority, -best) -> combined

dplyr::count(combined, source, keep)
dplyr::count(combined |> dplyr::filter(keep), property_type)
dplyr::count(combined |> dplyr::filter(keep), company)
readr::write_csv(combined, "data/combined_listings.csv")
```
